claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with:

**Do you have any children you're responsible for, and if so, how many?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I have one child - my daughter Alex. She's 8 years old and lives with me at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! It's helpful to know about Alex.

Now I need to ask you some questions to determine your eligibility:

**Do you currently live in the UK?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great, thank you. Next question:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do you live with her and/or pay for her food, clothes, and other needs?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. Alex lives with me and I'm responsible for her care - I provide everything she needs like food, clothes, and all her other needs.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. A couple more questions:

**Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for her.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent. Just a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in hospital, care, or any residential accommodation, or does she live at home with you full-time?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex has been in hospital for a while now - she's been there for a few months. It's been quite difficult for us.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to hear that Alex has been in hospital - that must be very difficult for you and your family.

I need to ask some follow-up questions about this:

**How many weeks has Alex been in hospital so far?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: She's been in hospital for 11 weeks now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks (which is under the 12-week threshold), this is an important detail.

One more question:

**Do you regularly spend money on Alex while she's in hospital - for example, on things like clothes, toys, books, or other items for her?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do. I still buy her clothes, magazines, and her favorite snacks and food. I want to make sure she has everything she needs while she's in there.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. I now have enough details to assess your eligibility.

Let me carefully consider your situation against the Child Benefit rules:

- You live in the UK ✓
- You have a child (Alex, age 8) who is under 16 ✓
- You are responsible for Alex's care - she normally lives with you and you provide for her needs ✓
- Nobody else is claiming Child Benefit for Alex ✓
- Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, which is under the 12-week limit
- You regularly spend money on Alex while she's in hospital ✓

Based on the rules, you would normally still be entitled to Child Benefit for a child in a UK hospital for up to 12 weeks. Since Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks and you are regularly spending money on her, you should still be eligible. However, it's important to note that if Alex remains in hospital beyond 12 weeks total, your eligibility may be affected unless you continue to regularly spend money on her (in which case an exception may apply).

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Assessment Complete

**Good news! You are ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:
- You meet all the basic requirements: you live in the UK, Alex is under 16 (she's 8), you're responsible for her care, and nobody else is claiming for her
- Although Alex has been in hospital for 11 weeks, this is still within the 12-week threshold
- Importantly, because you regularly spend money on Alex while she's in hospital (buying clothes, magazines, snacks and food), you would likely continue to be eligible even if her hospital stay extends beyond 12 weeks

**Important note:** If Alex's hospital stay does go beyond 12 weeks, you should contact HMRC to inform them of the situation. Because you're regularly spending money on her, an exception should apply and you should be able to continue receiving Child Benefit.

I hope Alex recovers soon and is able to come home. If you have any other questions about Child Benefit, feel free to ask!
